findings.issue: The app ships with no test script, runner, or devDependencies; nothing guards the data layer once the acceptance suite is no longer run against this code.
findings.suggestion: Add @nuxt/test-utils/vitest (or plain vitest) and unit tests for server/utils/pokeapi.ts helpers and the MoveTable comparator — these are pure functions/components and cheap to test.

findings.issue: The sort comparator handles nulls-last in both directions via early returns before the sign is applied; a small refactor (e.g. inlining sign into the null branches or reordering checks) breaks the spec's 'missing values sort last in both directions' rule with no failing test.
findings.suggestion: Table-driven unit tests over rows with null power/accuracy and both sort directions, asserting nulls stay last.

findings.issue: cardsFor encodes the core business rules (alternate forms ID > 10000 excluded, Pokémon→species name mapping, dedupe, dex-number sort). A regression here (e.g. forgetting deoxys-normal maps to species Deoxys) would silently corrupt every card list on move/ability/type pages.
findings.suggestion: Unit test cardsFor with a stubbed speciesNames map: alternate forms, duplicate refs, unknown-ID fallback, sort order.

findings.issue: latestFlavorText and englishShortEffect implement whitespace collapsing (\n, \f runs) and 'last English entry' selection; the humanize helper (two copies: here and app/app/utils/format.ts:4) has the hyphen-capitalization rule. All untested pure functions.
findings.suggestion: Unit tests with realistic fixtures (flavor text containing \f, mr-mime → 'Mr Mime', missing entries → null).

findings.issue: The `page` computed clamps out-of-range ?page= values for display but never syncs the URL, so /?q=char&page=99 renders 'Page 1 of N' while the URL still says 99; the 48-per-page slice math is also untested.
findings.suggestion: A component test covering clamping, empty results ('No Pokémon found'), and the last-page omission of 'Next page'.

findings.issue: Games are ordered by pairing gameRecords with [...gameNames][i] positional indexing against a Set's insertion order, and learn entries are deduped by a string key — fragile positional logic with no test.
findings.suggestion: Extract game ordering/dedupe into a testable function and test it (including duplicate version_group_details).

findings.issue: typesById is built by iterating type records and pushing per-Pokémon entries, then sorted by slot; if slot data is missing or ties occur the order falls back to type-iteration order, and species with no recorded types silently lose type filtering. Untested aggregation over 18 type records.
findings.suggestion: Unit test the aggregation with a small fixture (slots out of order, alternate forms present, a species with no types).

findings.issue: The 404/500 propagation logic (statusCode fallback, fatal error, useFetch key/dedupe) is only exercised end-to-end by acceptance tests; the non-404 error branch appears untested anywhere.
findings.suggestion: A test mounting a page whose server route 500s, asserting the error page heading.

findings.issue: The 60s in-memory cache (TTL_MS, rejection cleanup, size eviction) is untested; a bug in cache eviction or the rejection path would cause stale data or poisoned entries.
findings.suggestion: Unit tests for cache hit/miss/expiry/rejected-promise removal; consider injecting fetch for determinism.

findings.issue: humanize is duplicated between app/utils/format.ts and server/utils/pokeapi.ts:37-41; the two copies can drift (they differ only in non-null assertion style) and neither is tested.
findings.suggestion: Share one implementation via a module usable by both server and app (e.g. app/utils auto-imported or a shared/ dir) and unit test it.

summary: The app contains no tests of its own — no runner, script, or devDependencies — leaving its riskiest logic (Pokémon/species card mapping, move-table sorting, filter/pagination state, flavor-text normalization) guarded only by the external acceptance suite. That logic is mostly pure and easily unit-testable, so the gap is cheap to close and expensive to leave: any refactor of the data layer would ship silently. Code quality elsewhere is decent, which makes the total absence of tests the one clear, high-severity review blocker.
